extracted.intended_audience: physicians, medical societies, health policy stakeholders, and federal policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: A summary of AMA federal advocacy actions, legislative positions, and regulatory requests relevant to Medicare Advantage prior authorization, FDA digital health pilots, Medicare coverage determinations for pain procedures, and the HIPAA Security Proposed Rule. Intended to inform and mobilize physicians and stakeholder organizations for notice-and-comment and legislative outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require MA plans to implement electronic prior authorization programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Require MA plans to implement electronic prior authorization programs that adhere to newly developed federal standards and are capable of seamlessly integrating into electronic health systems (vs. proprietary health plan portals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a way to reduce physician administrative burden and unnecessary delays in patient care; ties to a bipartisan bill (Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act) and a 2018 consensus statement developed by stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate reporting by plans to CMS on prior authorization use and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandate that plans report to CMS on the extent of their use of prior authorization and the rate of approvals and denials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to increase transparency and allow CMS and Congress to assess the impact and prevalence of prior authorization in Medicare Advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create pathway for real-time decisions for routinely approved items/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a pathway for CMS to study and institute real-time decisions for routinely approved items and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks to accelerate access for items/services that are routinely approved, reducing delays caused by manual prior authorization processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify CMS authority to set timeframes for electronic prior authorization approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify CMS’ authority to establish timeframes for electronic prior authorization request approvals, including expedited deadlines for emergent services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds enforceable timelines (including expedited handling for emergencies) to ensure timely patient care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require HHS and agencies to report to Congress on program integrity and improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and other agencies to report to Congress on program integrity efforts and other ways to further improve the electronic prior authorization process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures oversight and iterative improvement of the electronic prior authorization framework through mandated reporting to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEMPO pilot: voluntary risk-based enforcement and data-collection requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the FDA TEMPO pilot, devices intended to provide care under the ACCESS model may request FDA enforcement discretion for certain requirements (such as pre-market review); if granted enforcement discretion, manufacturers must collect, monitor, and report real-world performance data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot is voluntary and risk-based; developed with CMS to support the ACCESS model. Eligible devices include those intended to improve cardio-kidney-metabolic, musculoskeletal, and behavioral health conditions. The real-world data reporting is intended to help FDA and CMS understand technology performance in clinical settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support ACCESS model to enable technology-supported chronic care
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the ACCESS model, a voluntary initiative to test technology-supported care for Medicare beneficiaries with chronic conditions, to bring new digital health tools into everyday care for Medicare patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMA will monitor implementation of both ACCESS and TEMPO and supports efforts that allow greater incorporation of innovative technologies into clinical care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind LCDs for Peripheral Nerve Blocks and chronic pain procedures to avoid patient harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Urge CMS to rescind proposed Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) for Peripheral Nerve Blocks (PNBs) and Procedures for Chronic Pain to avoid patient harm and preserve physicians’ ability to provide optimal pain care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter argues that restricting evidence-based PNBs would force physicians to use suboptimal alternatives (including opioids), increasing patient risk and potential complications. Examples of PNBs cited: Greater Occipital Nerve Blocks, Stellate Ganglion Block, Sympathetic Blocks, Lateral Femoral Cutaneous Nerve Blocks, Ilioinguinal and Iliohypogastric Nerve Blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct MACs to rescind LCDs to prevent ethical/clinical compromise
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask CMS to direct multiple Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs) to rescind the LCDs so that physicians are not placed in a potentially ethically and clinically compromised position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames rescission as necessary to protect clinicians’ ability to recommend evidence-based care and to avoid forcing less-optimal or riskier treatments on patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid imposing substantial new financial burdens and unreasonable timelines in HIPAA Security updates
rubrics_metrics.description: The HIPAA Security Proposed Rule, as drafted, would impose substantial new financial burdens on providers and includes unreasonable implementation timelines that are difficult to reconcile with the IT complexities of modern health care delivery organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMA contends the proposal should not be finalized in its current form and that implementation timelines and costs must be reasonable given diverse provider IT environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIPAA Security Rule updates must be flexible and allow innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any update to health care cybersecurity standards must be flexible enough to accommodate a wide range of provider organizations and set strong protections that allow providers opportunities to innovate to respond effectively to evolving cybersecurity risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates for balancing robust privacy/security protections with flexibility so providers of different sizes and capabilities can comply and innovate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use collaborative outreach with providers and regulated entities to craft HIPAA updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage HHS to conduct a collaborative outreach initiative with providers and other regulated entities to produce a HIPAA Security Rule that offers more robust protections but is less burdensome and costly for health care providers and stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMA joined a coalition asking HHS to withdraw the Proposed Rule and instead engage stakeholders to co-develop practicable, less-burdensome regulatory language; the AMA previously submitted detailed comment letter recommending substantial revisions.
